payload.summary: resolved_dispatch_lane() in scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq (used by SLS/RLC promote scripts) has no zone=="multi" special-case. When a row has zone=multi (per docs/agents/po/flow/main.md:30, 'multi (architect must split)') but no structured next_agent/owner field, the resolver's generic fallback silently defaults to "developer" instead of "architect" -- contradicting the canonical zone=multi routing rule even when a PO ruling explicitly states architect must split.
payload.live_incident: FIX-PUSH-DELIVERY-ERROR-RATE-ALERT (2026-08-08T02:22Z SLS claim) -- row carries po_ruling_20260730 explicitly stating 'ARCHITECT SPLITS IT' for this exact reason (zone=multi), but had no next_agent field set, so SLS resolved dispatch_lane=developer. Router caught this via RAW-verification before spawning and hand-corrected the row's next_agent/dispatch_lane to architect (see row's own router_dispatch_correction_20260808T0223Z field) -- a row-level patch, not a systemic fix.
payload.suggested_fix: resolved_dispatch_lane($detail_items) in scripts/lib/devteam-eligibility.jq should check .zone == "multi" BEFORE falling back to the generic "developer" default, and resolve to "architect" in that case (still deferring to an explicit next_agent/owner field if present, same precedence order as today).
payload.scope_note: Same class of defect as the adjacent 'prose-sequencing-without-machine-encoding guard' already in this file (PO prose rulings not backed by a machine-readable field get silently ignored by automated resolvers) -- worth checking whether other resolver defs in this file have the same blind spot for zone=multi rows.
